# Personalized Marketing Agent — Production Runbook

> **Scenario**: Personalized Marketing Agent
> **Platform**: Microsoft Copilot Studio — GitHub Copilot harness
> **Target readers**: Makers, delivery engineers, customer or partner operators

**Estimated effort**: Not yet measured; record actual effort on the Frontier Clock.

**Template:** an example to modify for your requirements; the customer or partner wires it into their environment. See the [Overview](1.Overview.md).

## Prerequisites

| Requirement | Details | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build workload | 18 captured build checkpoints; 4 skills; 2 knowledge files; 6 acceptance checks; 4 locked cases. [Inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components), [checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks), and [cases](4.Sample-prompts.md#demo-prompts). | Template |
| Licensing and capacity | Confirm licensing for your tenant and Copilot Credits for the GitHub Copilot harness; building, Preview and evaluation consume credits before publication. | Customer or partner |
| Environment and maker access | Record the approved marketing environment, publisher prefix and maker access; confirm the reviewed Sonnet46 model is available and keep the workshop Draft. | Customer or partner |
| DLP and data policy | Have the administrator review uploaded marketing knowledge, the proposed CRM or insights feed, Teams review and campaign workflow connections, and channel limits; document blocked paths. | Customer or partner |
| Identity and audience | Review the supplied GroupMembership access policy, Integrated authentication and Always trigger; record who may build, test and later use the agent. | Customer or partner |
| Connection ownership | Name owners for the read-only CRM or customer-insights feed and the campaign review workflow, with least-privilege references; the synthetic workshop needs none. | Customer or partner |
| Test identities | Prepare Marketing Director, Campaign Manager and denied-access identities for an approved test deployment; makers use Draft Preview. | Customer or partner |
| Tooling by build lane | Manual lane: the Copilot Studio browser and reviewed files. Easy mode: VS Code Agent mode, the Microsoft Copilot Studio plugin and a supported PAC CLI. | Customer or partner |
| Aggregate data approval | Have the marketing owner confirm that only authorized aggregate production data, after governance review, replaces the synthetic records. | Customer or partner |

## Phase 0 — Qualify and Adapt the Template

### Step 0-1. Qualify the outcome and baseline

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing business owner

Complete the [qualification checklist](1.Overview.md#qualification-checklist).

**Measure:** Campaign planning, content review and performance-insight steps by campaign, as run today Establish how planning, content review and measurement work today before attributing change to the adapted agent.

Fill your baseline record:

| Campaign | Target segment | Planning steps | Review and approval points | Content variants reviewed | Measurement source | Insight availability | Owner |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |

Agree replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures before production.

### Step 0-2. Adapt scope and name owners

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing business owner

Adapt [scope](1.Overview.md#in-scope--out-of-scope) and the [data contract](2.Architecture.md#data-contract); assign approval roles.

| Role | Responsibility |
| --- | --- |
| Marketing business owner | Approve data sources, privacy boundaries, success measures and publication; the Marketing Director retains audience, offer and timing decisions. |
| Campaign reviewers | Review audience, copy, offer concepts, timing and measurement before any activation outside the agent. |
| Copilot Studio maker | Build the reviewed instructions, two knowledge files and four skills; remove web search, confirm the model and keep the owned agent Draft. |
| Power Platform administrator | Confirm tenant licensing, capacity, maker access, authenticated audience and data policies before any marketing connection is approved. |
| CRM and review connection owners | Approve the read-only CRM or customer-insights feed and the campaign review workflow; record each connection identity and least-privilege reference. |
| Acceptance reviewer | Check PM-01 through PM-04, the boundary tests and Easy/Manual parity; reject evidence lacking its markers or Draft state. |
| Operations owner | Own production support, session and credit monitoring and configuration recovery; route marketing decisions to the authorized approvers. |

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Replacement connections, governance, telemetry, support and success measures are agreed before production.
- [ ] The marketing owner records current planning steps, content review points and measurement sources before agreeing success measures.

## Phase 1 — Environment, Identity and Access

### Step 1-1. Approve the identity and settings design

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Review and approve the [identity design](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions) and [template settings](../../solutions/personalized-marketing/copilot-studio/settings.mcs.yml). Apply agent-specific settings when the agent is built in [Phase 2](#phase-2--build-and-prove-the-agent).

Approve document, connector and channel policies; require authentication and verify blocked routes stay blocked.

### Step 1-2. Configure tenant controls

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Approve the environment, audience and connection identities. Define the [authentication plan](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication); configure environment [data policies](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/admin-data-loss-prevention).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The target environment and approved publisher prefix are recorded before any build lane starts.
- [ ] The authentication option, required sign-in and allowed audience are approved for aggregate marketing data.

## Phase 2 — Build and Prove the Agent

### Step 2-1. Choose the build lane

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

| Lane | Suits | Output |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Easy mode with GitHub Copilot (default) | Assisted authoring | Synthetic Draft proof |
| Manual build in Copilot Studio | Browser-only makers | Same Draft proof |
| AIBAST Frontier (experimental) | Portable learning | Behavior proof; native validation follows |

[Compare lanes](1.Overview.md#delivery-lanes); local Brainstem remains optional.

### Step 2-2. Build the selected implementation

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

**Easy mode:** use the [authoring skill](../../skills/aibast-easy-mode-copilot/SKILL.md) and [reviewed messages](../../solutions/personalized-marketing/EASY-MODE-COPILOT-CHAT.md). **Manual:** use the [single inventory](2.Architecture.md#copilot-studio-components) and [tutorial](https://microsoft.github.io/aibast-agents-library/solutions/personalized-marketing/manual-tutorial.html) with the checklist below. **Portable learning:** follow [deployment.json](../../solutions/personalized-marketing/deployment.json); it does not replace native Draft validation.

**Manual build checklist** — [captured sequence](../../solutions/personalized-marketing/screenshots/manual/browserfilm.json). Record current results.

1. Create a blank Copilot Studio agent
2. Name Personalized Marketing Manual
3. Enter the reviewed global instructions
4. Save the instruction policy
5. Remove default web search
6. Add knowledge: aibast_personalized-marketing-rules-and-safety.md
7. Add knowledge: aibast_personalized-marketing-synthetic-records.md
8. Add skill: campaign-design
9. Add skill: content-personalization
10. Add skill: customer-segmentation
11. Add skill: performance-analysis
12. Review model, skills, knowledge, and safety boundaries
13. Open a fresh Preview conversation
14. Pass PM-01: Marketing Director
15. Pass PM-02: Campaign Manager
16. Pass PM-03: Campaign Manager
17. Pass PM-04: Marketing Director
18. Confirm Draft and stop before publish

### Step 2-3. Enforce workshop integrity

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Apply the [workshop integrity and recovery rules](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) before replay.

### Step 2-4. Replay the synthetic proof

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

**Synthetic demo acceptance:** record every locked case: PM-01, PM-02, PM-03, PM-04. Use the [acceptance matrix](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [template acceptance checks](0.Resources/README.md#template-acceptance-checks).

### Exit criteria

- [ ] This lane's Preview evidence identifies the agent, environment, model, inventory, cases and Draft state.
- [ ] If Easy mode is chosen, the source-controlled project uses cli-copilot in the approved environment and stays Draft.
- [ ] If the portable lane is chosen, the recipe smoke test calls `PersonalizedMarketingAgent` and returns `Total Addressable Customers`.
- [ ] The manual build has reviewed instructions, two knowledge files, four skills and the confirmed model; web search and tools are absent.
- [ ] Each unchanged locked prompt passes in its own fresh Preview conversation on the owned Draft.
- [ ] Case passes rest on the deterministic validator; an annotated image is a learner checkpoint, not the machine gate.
- [ ] Any Easy/Manual comparison uses identical instructions, knowledge, skills, model and case identifiers.

## Phase 3 — Wire In Your Systems

<a id="shared-integration-controls"></a>

**Shared identity and scope controls**

For each integration, decide end-user versus approved maker/service credentials. [Configure authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/configuration-end-user-authentication) for the [authorized audience](2.Architecture.md#identity-and-permissions).

**Shared scope:** Require sign-in before exposing segment, campaign or performance data. Request only the scopes needed for approved aggregate sources and review actions. Restrict the allowed audience and verify access with authorized and denied identities. Enforce these restrictions at each connection.

### Step 3-1. Integrate Approved read-only CRM or customer-insights feed

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM and review connection owners

1. **Bind Approved read-only CRM or customer-insights feed — read:** Bind scoped read-only connector or API actions for aggregate data only.

2. **Identity for Approved read-only CRM or customer-insights feed:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved read-only CRM or customer-insights feed:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved read-only CRM or customer-insights feed:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 3](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not identify or profile a person; summarize aggregate segment signals only. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Stop and request a valid synthetic identifier; do not approximate.

### Step 3-2. Integrate Approved campaign review workflow

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM and review connection owners

1. **Bind Approved campaign review workflow — write:** Gate an approval workflow behind authorization and keep activation out of it (preview).

2. **Identity for Approved campaign review workflow:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Approved campaign review workflow:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Approved campaign review workflow:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not send, schedule or launch; return the draft sequence and the human approval gate. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return drafts or recommendations, name the human approval gate and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-3. Integrate Microsoft Teams for human review

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM and review connection owners

1. **Bind Microsoft Teams for human review — read-write:** Start read-only; gate any posting or approval workflow behind approval (preview).

2. **Identity for Microsoft Teams for human review:** Follow the [shared controls](#shared-integration-controls); record the credential choice.

3. **Scope Microsoft Teams for human review:** Apply the [shared restrictions](#shared-integration-controls); document system-specific limits.

4. **Exit test for Microsoft Teams for human review:** Record expected and actual results on approved fixtures. [Boundary case 1](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases): Do not send, schedule or launch; return the draft sequence and the human approval gate. [Recovery](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery): Return drafts or recommendations, name the human approval gate and state that no side effect occurred.

### Step 3-4. Connect

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** CRM and review connection owners

Bind only approved read-only connections and keep sends, offers and launches in separate governed workflows.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] Approved connections preserve the reviewed input and output contract; no live lookup, sent message or approval is claimed without tool evidence.
- [ ] Only approved read-only connections are bound, and any write action stays separate.

## Phase 4 — Evaluate on Your Data

### Step 4-1. Adapt the evaluation corpus

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Preserve [locked behaviors](4.Sample-prompts.md#per-case-acceptance-matrix) and [boundary tests](4.Sample-prompts.md#routing-and-boundary-cases) when substituting approved customer fixtures.

### Step 4-2. Set thresholds and evaluate your data

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

Have the business owner approve thresholds. Run [adapted evaluations (preview)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-agent-evaluation-intro) before publication under approved test user profiles. Keep exact assertions separate from General quality scores.

Test an approved deployment as intended marketing users and an unshared identity; maker access does not prove user connection access.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The marketing owner sets customer-data acceptance measures; synthetic lift, revenue and ROAS figures are not thresholds.
- [ ] Adapted evaluations identify the tested version and user profile; General quality scoring does not replace exact assertions.

## Phase 5 — Pilot and Rollout

### Step 5-1. Review the template release prerequisites

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Acceptance reviewer

These synthetic regression gates do not set production thresholds. The reference workshop stays Draft; production approval belongs to the customer pilot.

| Template gate | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Locked marketing corpus | All four cases, PM-01 through PM-04, return every required marker. |
| Manual inventory | Two knowledge files, four skills and the reviewed model; web search removed and no tools. |
| Privacy and activation boundary | Any sensitive profiling, sent or scheduled message, offer, reward, launch or purchase is no-go. |
| Visual checkpoint acceptance | Require a visible positive anchor without a blocker or refusal; withhold reshoot-required captures. |
| Release state | The owned workshop agent is Draft with `published: false`. |

### Step 5-2. Publish and share deliberately

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing business owner

With business approval, [publish and share](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent) the adapted build with a restricted test audience. Keep the reference workshop Draft.

Require explicit confirmation before the production publish operation.

### Step 5-3. Run the governed pilot

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Marketing business owner

**Pilot entry gate:** Test allowed and denied identities on the published, shared agent; resolve access failures before admitting pilot users. Compare pilot results with the baseline and thresholds; broaden rollout only after go/no-go.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The production publish operation has explicit human confirmation.
- [ ] The approved marketing audience and supported channels are configured and tested before publication.

## Phase 6 — Operate

### Step 6-1. Retain the operational playbook

**Owner:** Template · **Role:** Operations owner

The template provides the [state-and-recovery playbook](2.Architecture.md#state-and-recovery) and regression cases.

### Step 6-2. Own changes and ongoing verification

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Operations owner

Review content freshness and permissions; re-evaluate source, model, skill or connector changes. [Monitor the deployed agent](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/analytics-overview).

Review marketing session transcripts, failed interactions, connection errors and credit usage in Monitor.

### Step 6-3. Release: ALM

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Copilot Studio maker

Back up the reviewed workspace, pull before editing and pushing, then package with `pac copilot pack`.

### Step 6-4. Release: recovery

**Owner:** Customer or partner · **Role:** Power Platform administrator

Confirm backup eligibility for the environment type and rehearse restoration to a supported test target.

### Exit criteria

- [ ] The recovery rehearsal uses a restore path supported for the environment type and target.
- [ ] The operator reviews failed sessions, source usage, connection errors and credit consumption after rollout.

- [ ] Build-to-operate playbooks and integrity rules.

### Customer or partner delivers

- [ ] Customer-data results, thresholds and go/no-go.
- [ ] Approved publication, operations and recovery.
